task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2c) on REQ-167's implementation, commit 69e8722 on lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex and lib/letflow/application.ex. REQ-167's own text explicitly names SECURITY-REVIEWER as a hard gate -- 'This is the sandbox boundary for guest code.' Read the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req167-wasm-import-whitelist.md) and the real diff (git show 69e8722) in full before verdict. This is the WASM authorization boundary: build_import_table/1 constructs a manifest-driven whitelist and start_instance/2 instantiates a guest module against exactly that table, denying anything outside it (including all filesystem/WASI access, since the registry has zero filesystem entries and no wasi: option is ever supplied).
acceptance_criteria: Confirm build_import_table/1 is a genuine whitelist by construction (filter-then-group, never allow-everything-then-remove) -- read the real code, not just the design's claim about itself.

Confirm start_instance/2 never supplies a wasi: option to Wasmex.start_link/1 under any manifest input, and that no manifest content can cause a filesystem-shaped import to appear in the built table (the @known_imports registry must contain zero filesystem-shaped entries) -- this is the WASM-07 guarantee and the most security-critical property in this diff.

Confirm a module importing anything outside the built whitelist genuinely fails to instantiate (never resolves to a callable host function) -- verify this is a real instantiation-time failure, not a runtime error on first call.

Confirm the instantiation attempt genuinely runs inside Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 under the new CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor, never inline, containing the same crash-propagation hazard REQ-165/166 already found in this codebase's use of Wasmex.start_link/1.

Confirm start_instance/2's successful {:ok, pid} branch does NOT stop the returned instance (unlike ModuleRegistry's stage-2 proving instance) -- this is an intentional design difference (design section 3); confirm the design's own rationale (this is the real instance a caller intends to invoke against) is sound and doesn't leave the caller without a way to clean it up, and that no other code path in this module leaks a second, uncleaned-up instance.

Confirm the placeholder @known_imports registry's two entries (var:read/read_variable, service:call/platform_call_service) are genuinely inert stub callbacks (return a constant, no real side effect) -- since no real host-function semantics exist yet, confirm nothing here is prematurely exposing a real capability.

Cross-check against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8 explicitly -- INV-3 (untrusted-runtime sandboxing) is squarely this diff's subject matter, more directly than REQ-165/166's SECURITY-REVIEWER passes.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

`git diff main...69e8722 --stat` confirms lib/letflow/engine/wasm/module_registry.ex and plugin_handler.ex are absent from the diff -- genuinely untouched
`mix compile --warnings-as-errors` run live (asdf-installed elixir/erlang, PATH including .asdf/shims and .cargo/bin): clean, zero output, zero warnings

`WASMEX_BUILD=true mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate_test.exs` run live: 'Result: 16 passed', 0 failures -- includes real Wasmex NIF instantiation attempts against the WAT fixtures, not mocked

read all four priv/wasm_fixtures/req167_*.wat fixtures directly: each's actual import declaration matches what its corresponding test claims it does (platform_call_service-only, wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open with the real 9-param/1-result signature, an entirely unregistered import name, and a no-imports module)

grepped lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex for `wasi` outside comments/moduledoc prose: the only executable code path calling Wasmex.start_link/1 passes exactly %{bytes: bytes, imports: table} -- no :wasi key is ever constructed or supplied, under any manifest input

read @known_imports (capability_gate.ex lines 177-192) directly: exactly two entries, both namespace "env" (read_variable, platform_call_service) -- zero wasi_snapshot_preview1 or other filesystem-shaped entries exist in the registry for any manifest content to select

read build_import_table/1 (lines 202-217): Enum.filter (membership test) then Enum.reduce (group into the namespace/name map) -- a genuine filter-then-group construction, never an allow-everything-then-remove one; no other code path builds or supplements the returned table

read start_instance/2 (lines 241-263): the only Wasmex.start_link/1 call in the module is inside Task.Supervisor.async_nolink(@task_supervisor, fn -> ... end) where @task_supervisor = Letflow.Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor; register/1-equivalent inline call does not exist. Success branch ({:ok, {:ok, pid}} -> {:ok, pid}) performs no GenServer.stop and no second instantiation -- single success path, no second leaked instance possible from this function
read stub_callback/0 (lines 271-274): `fn _context, _arg1, _arg2 -> 0 end` -- a constant-returning function with no side effect, no I/O, no state access

read application.ex diff: appends exactly one new Task.Supervisor child (CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor) after the existing ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor entry; no other child's spec, order, or restart strategy touched
acceptance_criteria_findings: 1. CONFIRMED: build_import_table/1 is a genuine whitelist by construction -- Enum.filter(&MapSet.member?(granted, &1.capability)) keeps only manifest-granted descriptors, then Enum.reduce groups survivors into the namespace/name map. No branch constructs a full table and removes entries; the filter runs first.

2. CONFIRMED (the most security-critical property in this diff, verified at multiple levels): (a) source-level grep shows no :wasi key is ever constructed anywhere in this file; (b) the only Wasmex.start_link/1 call site passes literally %{bytes: bytes, imports: table}; (c) @known_imports has exactly two entries, both under the "env" namespace, zero filesystem-shaped or wasi_snapshot_preview1 entries -- so no manifest.capabilities content, however permissive, can cause build_import_table/1 to emit a filesystem-shaped key; (d) live test run confirms req167_path_open.wat (real wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open import, 9-param/1-result signature) is rejected identically under an empty manifest AND under a manifest granting every capability the registry defines -- proving the denial is structural (registry has nothing to grant), not merely a manifest that happened not to ask for it.

3. CONFIRMED as a genuine instantiation-time failure, not a first-call runtime error: the AC1 test (req167_platform_call_only.wat, manifest granting only var:read) returns {:error, {:instantiation_denied, {:unresolved_import, "env", "platform_call_service"}}} -- this is Wasmex.start_link/1 itself crashing while resolving the module's import section (a NIF-level linking failure), before any function of the module is ever called or a pid is ever produced. No test in this suite invokes a granted host function through a live instance at all (confirmed by reading every test), so 'fails to instantiate' cannot be conflated with 'fails when called' here -- there is no call path exercised that could blur the two.

4. CONFIRMED via live test run: the Wasmex.start_link/1 attempt happens exclusively inside Task.Supervisor.async_nolink(@task_supervisor, fn -> ... end), @task_supervisor = Letflow.Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor, a new supervisor added to application.ex distinct from ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor/PluginTaskSupervisor/Lua.TaskSupervisor. The AC1 'does not crash the calling test process' test passed live (16/16, including this one) -- an inline call on the same unresolved-import fixture would have exited the linked test process before that assertion could run, per the identical crash-propagation hazard REQ-165/166 already documented and this module's own moduledoc restates.

5. CONFIRMED, and the design's own rationale is sound: start_instance/2's only success branch ({:ok, {:ok, pid}} -> {:ok, pid}) does not call GenServer.stop -- verified by reading the full function body, which contains no stop/kill call on any branch except the timeout path's Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill) (which only ever fires when start_link has NOT produced a live pid). This differs correctly from ModuleRegistry's stage-2 proving instance, which exists solely to prove instantiability and is thrown away; here the returned pid is the real, intended instance the design states the caller must invoke against and must GenServer.stop/1 itself. No other code path in this module constructs a second Wasmex instance -- start_instance/2 contains exactly one Wasmex.start_link/1 call site -- so there is no second, uncleaned-up instance this module could leak. The caller-owns-cleanup contract is stated plainly in the @doc, not left implicit.

6. CONFIRMED: both @known_imports entries' callbacks are stub_callback/0, `fn _context, _arg1, _arg2 -> 0 end` -- a constant return, no side effect, no state, no I/O, no delegation to any other module. Neither read_variable nor platform_call_service does anything beyond returning 0 regardless of arguments; nothing here exposes a real capability ahead of REQ-171/172, matching the moduledoc's own 'placeholder registry, not a resolved host-API vocabulary' framing.
7. See invariant_crosscheck below -- INV-3 addressed explicitly and in more depth than REQ-165/166's passes, per this handoff's own framing.
invariant_crosscheck: INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. `git diff main...69e8722 --stat` touches no priv/repo/migrations/*.exs, no Ecto schema, no Repo call, no tenant-scoped table (confirmed: `grep -n "Repo\.\|schema \|use Ecto" lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex` returns no hits). This module persists nothing -- it builds an in-memory map and instantiates bytes in-process, returning a bare pid. INV-1's preconditions (a diff touching a tenant-scoped table/schema/migration) are not met.
INV-2 (server-side field authorisation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response type or serialization boundary touched; S4 has not started.

INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing) -- APPLIES and is SATISFIED. `docs/migration/decisions/0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md` is the S5 build-vs-bind decision record INV-3's own text names as its precondition, and it is REVIEWER-signed-off (2026-08-23, per docs/migration/stage-5-scripting-plugins.md) -- so, correcting REQ-166's SECURITY-REVIEWER pass (which treated INV-3 as deferred because it read the decision record as not yet existing at the time it ran, on the same calendar date this decision record's sign-off predates), INV-3 is live for this diff and this diff is squarely its subject matter: this IS the explicit host-capability allowlist mechanism INV-3's rule text calls for. Verified against INV-3's exact rule clauses: (a) 'no host function reachable unless the script's granted capability set names it' -- build_import_table/1's filter-then-group construction (AC1/AC2 above) is exactly this, structurally proven rather than asserted; (b) 'no ambient filesystem access' -- zero filesystem-shaped registry entries and no :wasi option ever supplied, verified at the source level and exercised live against the real wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open surface under both an empty and a maximally-permissive manifest; (c) 'no ambient network access' -- @known_imports contains no network-shaped entry (its two entries are read_variable and platform_call_service, both inert stubs per AC6 above) and no other code path in this module could resolve one. This diff does not implement the full future host-API vocabulary (that is explicitly out of scope, per the design's own §8 open questions and moduledoc's AC6 statement), but the allowlist *mechanism* INV-3 requires is real, live-tested, and structurally exhaustive for everything currently registrable.

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. `grep -niE "(password|secret|client_secret|token)\s*(=|:)\s*\"[^\"]{8,}\"" lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex lib/letflow/application.ex` returns no hits; no secret material is read, logged, or threaded through this diff.
INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No lookup-by-ID endpoint; S4 has not started.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- satisfied by this handoff itself: SECURITY-REVIEWER handoff with status PASS and an explicit per-invariant statement, per INV-6's own how-to-verify.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. `grep -rn "Repo.query" lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex lib/letflow/application.ex` returns no hits; this diff contains no SQL of any kind.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES and is SATISFIED. `grep -n "^\s*{:ok, .*} = " lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex` has no hit; start_instance/2's case covers every Task.yield/2 outcome ({:ok,{:ok,pid}}, {:ok,{:error,reason}}, {:exit,reason}, nil/timeout) with a typed result. The one place a raw external crash is genuinely allowed to occur (Wasmex.start_link/1 on an unresolved import) is deliberately isolated inside Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2, specifically so it cannot propagate to the calling process -- verified live by the passing crash-propagation-containment test, not just by reading the code.

result.verdict_summary: PASS. INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5, INV-7 NOT-APPLICABLE (no tenant table/migration/schema/secret/SQL/lookup-endpoint touched); INV-3 APPLIES and is SATISFIED -- this diff is squarely the host-capability-allowlist mechanism INV-3 requires, now checkable because the S5 decision record (0014) exists and is REVIEWER-signed-off, correcting REQ-166's prior pass which treated INV-3 as still deferred; INV-6 satisfied by this handoff; INV-8 APPLIES and is SATISFIED, verified live via the crash-containment test.
